items.title: Cortisol in cardio-kidney-metabolic disease.
items.abstract: Despite guideline-directed therapy, many patients with cardio-kidney-metabolic (CKM) disease remain uncontrolled due to therapeutic inertia, adherence barriers, and underrecognized secondary causes. Hypercortisolism, ranging from mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) to overt Cushing syndrome, is an increasingly recognized contributor. MACS is associated with a 2.5-fold higher risk of cardiovascular death and increased prevalence of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and kidney impairment. Cortisol excess promotes muscle insulin resistance, hepatic gluconeogenesis, β-cell dysfunction, sodium retention, and vascular remodelling, worsening glycaemia and blood pressure, leading to poor CKM outcomes. Recent prospective studies suggest that hypercortisolism is more prevalent than previously suspected in selected CKM phenotypes, including 24% in patients with difficult-to-control T2DM in CATALYST and 27% in patients with resistant hypertension in MOMENTUM. The overnight 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test remains the diagnostic test of choice. Therapeutic strategies include adrenal steroidogenesis inhibitors, glucocorticoid receptor antagonists, and pituitary-directed therapies in selected cases, while surgery remains the first-line treatment for surgically remediable disease. This review summarizes the epidemiology and mechanisms linking cortisol excess to CKM dysfunction, and also highlights the need for clinical trials, standardized diagnostic thresholds, and assays to enable integration of cortisol-targeted therapies into management pathways to mitigate residual CKM risk. This review will serve as a practical guide for cardiologists to manage a potentially reversible contributor to poor CKM control.

Positive Impact of Hypertension in Patients with Early-stage Lung Cancer Treated With Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy.
items.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the effect of hypertension on recurrence and progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with early-stage lung cancer who underwent curative stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). This study included 100 patients with T1-T3N0M0 lung cancer who underwent lung SBRT using CyberKnife or volumetric-modulated arc therapy at Inha University Hospital between July 2008 and June 2025. Recurrence rates and PFS were analyzed. Data on hypertension and specific types of antihypertensive medications were retrospectively reviewed from electronic medical records. The median follow-up period was 31.0 months (range=0.7-136.7 months). Of the 100 patients, 52 had hypertension. Recurrence occurred in 38 patients, including 25 with locoregional failure and 13 with distant metastases. Recurrence rates were significantly lower in patients with hypertension ( p =0.015), with reduced locoregional recurrence ( p =0.022), whereas distant metastasis showed no significant correlation with hypertension ( p =0.315). Hypertensive drug users (n=37) had lower recurrence rates ( p =0.003). Recurrence was higher in male patients ( p =0.049) and lower in those aged >70 years ( p =0.033). Patients with hypertension showed significantly improved PFS ( p =0.010) but no difference in overall survival based on hypertension status ( p =0.319). Other factors that positively affected PFS included female sex and age >70 years. Patients actively receiving antihypertensive medication showed greater PFS than those who did not ( p =0.016). In particular, those using beta-blockers showed a low recurrence rate (0%, p =0.033). The therapeutic effects of lung SBRT appear more pronounced in patients with hypertension. This favorable outcome may be related to the administration of antihypertensive medications, suggesting the need for further investigation into the underlying mechanisms.

items.title: From Controversy to Clarity: The New Landscape of Pediatric Autoimmune Hepatitis Care.
items.abstract: Over the past decade, there have been advancements in our knowledge of the pathogenesis of autoimmune hepatitis (AIH), resulting in diagnostic and prognostic biomarker discoveries and an expansion of treatment options. This article cites recent literature to aid clinicians in the understanding and awareness of diagnostic and treatment pitfalls and strategies. An overview of the current understanding of the immunopathogenesis of AIH, the diagnostic strategies to effectively exclude other chronic liver diseases, the evidence for emerging diagnostic and therapeutic biomarkers, and the management strategies for typical and difficult to treat cases is provided.

items.title: TIM-3 Up-regulation Is Associated With Altered Cytotoxic Function of Allogeneic Vγ9Vδ2 T Cells in Urinary Bladder Cancer.
items.abstract: γδ T cells, particularly the Vγ9Vδ2 subset, can recognize and directly kill cancer cells. γδ T-cell infusion can be autologous or allogeneic, but cancer cells employ various defense mechanisms against immune attack. This study evaluated the in vitro cytotoxic activity of patient-derived γδ T cells against urinary bladder cancer (UBC) cells and investigated TIM-3 expression and the effects of TIM-3 blockade on γδ T-cell cytotoxicity. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from UBC patients and healthy volunteers (HVs) were expanded ex vivo for 11 days and assessed for Vγ9Vδ2 T-cell expansion, differentiation, and cytotoxicity against cancer cells in vitro . Surface expression of checkpoint molecules on γδ T cells was also analyzed. Ex vivo -expanded γδ T cells from UBC patients expanded and differentiated into Vγ9Vδ2 T cells as efficiently as those from HVs but showed weaker cytotoxicity against UBC cells. TIM-3 was consistently and highly expressed throughout γδ T-cell expansion. Blocking TIM-3 signaling significantly increased the cytotoxicity of allogeneic HV-derived γδ T cells against UBC cells in vitro , although a similar effect was not observed in a small number of patient-derived samples tested. Ex vivo -expanded autologous γδ T cells from UBC patients expanded and differentiated normally but showed reduced cytotoxicity. Targeting TIM-3 enhanced the cytotoxicity of allogeneic Vγ9Vδ2 T cells in vitro , suggesting a promising strategy for improving allogeneic γδ T-cell-based immunotherapy for UBC; whether TIM-3 blockade similarly benefits patient-derived γδ T cells remains to be determined.

items.title: Integration of TRM-Cell Infiltration and PD-L1 Expression Improves Prognostic Stratification After Resection of NSCLC.
items.abstract: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, including tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells, are associated with prognosis in patients after resection of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, their clinical significance in the context of tumor immune suppression, such as through expression of programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1), remains unclear. We hypothesized that integrating TRM-cell infiltration with PD-L1 expression would improve prognostic stratification. We retrospectively analyzed 316 patients with NSCLC who underwent curative resection between 2017 and 2020 without perioperative immunotherapy. TRM cells were quantified by CD103 immunohistochemistry using tissue microarrays and digitally analyzed with QuPath. PD-L1 expression was assessed using the 22C3 assay. Recurrence was evaluated using competing-risks analysis. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox proportional hazards models. The median TRM density was 54.8 cells/mm 2 and was used to define TRM-high and TRM-low groups. TRM-high tumors were associated with non-adenocarcinoma histology and PD-L1 expression ≥1%. Patients with TRM-high tumors showed a significantly lower cumulative incidence of recurrence ( p =0.039), whereas PD-L1 expression ≥1% was associated with worse RFS and OS. When combined, TRM-high/PD-L1 expression p =0.017) and significantly improved RFS and OS ( p =0.0035 and p =0.0031, respectively). In multivariable analysis, TRM-high/PD-L1 expression <1% was independently associated with lower recurrence (hazard ratio=0.36) and improved RFS (hazard ratio=0.47). The combined assessment of TRM-cell infiltration and PD-L1 expression provides robust prognostic stratification in resected NSCLC and may serve as a useful biomarker for predicting postoperative outcomes.

items.title: Intravenous HER2-Targeted Vesicular Stomatitis Virus Infects and Cures Murine Mammary Tumors and Induces Anti-tumor Memory.
items.abstract: Vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) is a potent experimental oncolytic virus, but intravenous (IV) treatment is limited by rapid clearance and inefficient tumor delivery. This study investigated whether a HER2-targeted recombinant VSV could reach HER2-expressing tumors and produce therapeutic benefit after systemic administration. BALB/c mice bearing HER2-positive D2F2/E2 or parental D2F2 mammary tumors received a replicating recombinant VSV (rrVSV), IV rrVSV-G HER2, in which native low-density lipoprotein-receptor binding was 90% reduced by K47Q/R354Q substitutions and a HER2-specific single-chain antibody (SCA) was added to VSV-G. Tumor virus recovery, HER2 dependence, comparison with related viruses, effect of cyclophosphamide administration, survival after treatment of 3-day peritoneal tumors, and generation of anti-tumor T-cell immunity were examined. Preferential virus recovery in HER2-expressing tumors was greatest 3 days following IV administration. Tumor recovery from D2F2/E2 tumors expressing HER2 was markedly greater (4,482-fold) than from parental D2F2 tumors that did not express HER2. rrVSV-G HER2 gave much higher tumor virus recovery than did wild-type VSV (286-fold), a prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted control virus, or rrVSV-Sindbis HER2, an rrVSV in which the native G-glycoprotein (gp) was replaced by a targeted Sindbis gp. Treatment with IV rrVSV-G HER2 yielded cures in 44% (12 of 27) of mice bearing 3-day peritoneal D2F2/E2 tumors, when given in combination with anti-CTLA4 and cyclophosphamide. Long-term survivors developed anti-tumor T-cell immunity as shown by resistance to tumor rechallenge and the presence of HER2-specific tetramer-positive CD8 + T cells. Intravenously administered HER2-targeted VSV can preferentially infect HER2-expressing tumors, eliminate those tumors as part of combination immunotherapy, and generate anti-tumor memory T cells in a murine mammary tumor model.

items.title: Growth-Inhibitory Effects of the Rare Sugar D-allose in Renal Cell Carcinoma In Vitro and In Vivo .
items.abstract: Rare sugars are naturally occurring monosaccharides present only in trace amounts. This study investigated their potential to inhibit the growth of renal cell carcinoma (RCC), a malignancy that remains challenging to treat despite advances in targeted therapies and immunotherapies. Human RCC cell lines, including Caki-1, Caki-2, and ACHN, were exposed to eight rare sugars representing key intermediates of the Izumoring biosynthetic pathway, along with four common sugars as controls. Cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay. To further characterize D-allose, intracellular uptake of D-allose was analyzed by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and its antitumor efficacy was assessed in a xenograft mouse model. Among the sugars tested, D-allose reduced RCC cell viability across the tested concentrations. HPLC analysis detected intracellular D-allose in the examined RCC cells, supporting its intracellular availability under the experimental conditions. In vivo , D-allose significantly suppressed tumor growth in RCC xenograft-bearing mice without inducing apparent histological abnormalities in the liver or kidneys. Histopathological evaluation showed tumor necrosis as a qualitative observation in D-allose-treated tumors. These findings indicate that D-allose was detectable intracellularly in the examined RCC cells and inhibited RCC cell viability in vitro and tumor growth in vivo . Collectively, the results suggest that D-allose may represent a potential low-toxicity candidate for RCC therapy. Further studies are required to elucidate its molecular mechanisms, optimize dosing strategies, and evaluate its potential for clinical translation.

items.title: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis in Children: Unique Aspects and Approaches.
items.abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of pediatric autoimmune cholangiopathies, with particular emphasis on primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). It summarizes the epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, and natural history of these chronic immune-mediated liver diseases in children. Key aspects include the frequent overlap between PSC and autoimmune hepatitis, the strong association with inflammatory bowel disease, and current approaches to laboratory, imaging, and histological assessment. The challenges of disease monitoring and prognostication in pediatric PSC are highlighted. In addition, this review discusses current management strategies, advances in understanding disease pathogenesis, and ongoing efforts to develop effective disease-modifying therapies for affected children.

items.title: Emerging Role of Activated T cells in Pediatric Acute Liver Failure.
items.abstract: Activated T-cell hepatitis (TC-Hep) is an immune-mediated liver disease that presents in children aged 1 to 17 years with jaundice and high aminotransferases; severity ranges from severe hepatitis to acute liver failure (ALF). Many children previously labeled indeterminate ALF can be reclassified as TC-Hep. TC-Hep patients have liver tissue with diffuse portal and lobular CD8 T-cell inflammation and peripheral blood markers of T-cell activation. Treatment includes supportive care and consideration of immunosuppression, with optimal regimens yet to be determined. TC-Hep is not a chronic or recurrent disease, but patients are at a uniquely increased risk of developing aplastic anemia.

items.title: Prevalence of occult hepatitis B infection among blood donors from 2015 to 2025: A meta-analysis based on testing modalities and temporal trends.
items.abstract: Occult hepatitis B infection (OBI) remains an important concern for global blood safety. Published studies have reported inconsistent OBI prevalence among blood donors, and the influencing factors remain unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled OBI prevalence and explore potential sources of heterogeneity. We retrieved eligible studies published from 2015 to 2026. Pooled prevalence was calculated using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were conducted by testing method, study period, sample size, region, and national hepatitis B virus (HBV) screening conditions. Publication bias and result robustness were assessed via multiple statistical approaches. Significant between-study heterogeneity was identified. All subgroup analyses produced statistically significant interaction results (p for interaction ≤ 0.015). The prevalence of OBI varied remarkably across subgroups stratified by HBV-DNA testing method, research period, sample size, geographic region, national HBV endemicity, and blood screening level. The pooled OBI prevalence was higher in the 2023-2024 subgroup, although this likely reflects geographic confounding rather than a genuine temporal increase. No substantial publication bias was detected, and the overall pooled estimate was stable. High residual heterogeneity still persisted in all stratified subgroups. OBI is prevalent among global blood donors and affected by detection techniques, study period, sample size, region, and local screening capacity. Standardized molecular testing and long-term surveillance are recommended to reduce transfusion-transmitted HBV risks and ensure blood safety.

items.title: Lipidic obstruction of sinusoids (LOS): a potentially serious complication of steatotic liver disease.
items.abstract: During routine examination of specimens from patients with steatotic liver disease (SLD), we repeatedly observed a peculiar phenomenon characterized by obstruction of the hepatic sinusoids by lipid vacuoles (lipidic obstruction of sinusoids, LOS). These changes were reminiscent of pseudopeliotic steatosis (PPS), a complication following liver transplantation (LT), but notably occurred outside this context. The aim of our study was to identify diagnostic indicators for LOS and to determine its clinical significance. Liver specimens routinely sent to our institute between 2019 and 2024 with SLD were examined for LOS. The extracellular nature of the fat and the compression of the sinusoids were demonstrated by ancillary stains (Gomori, CD68, collagen IV). The extent of the LOS was quantified by measuring the area and maximum diameter of fat lakes. The clinical course of patients with LOS was retrospectively evaluated and correlated with the histological findings. LOS was observed in eight patients, ranging from focal to very extensive extracellular fat. The diagnosis was based on routine histology, supplemented by collagen IV stain highlighting double contours of sinusoids. The morphological findings suggested that lipidic obstruction of the hepatic sinusoids was a key pathophysiological factor. LOS was associated with liver necrosis and activation of macrophages. Patients with LOS exhibited a variable clinical course, ranging from subclinical to severe, including LT or even death. The extent of fat lakes correlated with the severity of the clinical course. We suggest the term LOS for a particular pattern of liver damage that can occur in SLD outside the transplantation setting and may lead to impaired hepatic blood flow. LOS is associated with a variable clinical presentation, ranging from subclinical to fatal. Clinicians and pathologists should be aware of this complication of SLD, which is diagnosed by liver histology.

items.title: UK national analysis of colonoscopy quality in inflammatory bowel disease surveillance: a National Endoscopy Database (NED) cohort study.
items.abstract: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) undergo colonoscopy for diagnosis, disease assessment, and colorectal cancer surveillance. We used the UK National Endoscopy Database (NED) to evaluate the quality of IBD surveillance and identify factors associated with procedural quality. All colonoscopies uploaded to NED between January 1 and December 31, 2024 were analyzed. IBD procedures were identified from recorded indications and classified as assessment or surveillance. Key performance indicators (KPIs) were assessed against national guidance. Case-mix-adjusted impacts of endoscopist- and service-level factors were evaluated using multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression. Of 588 841 colonoscopies, 2.7% (n = 15 971) were IBD surveillance. Although 56.8% of endoscopists performed at least one surveillance procedure, 18.9% performed one or more per month and delivered 57.1% of all surveillance. IBD surveillance quality was high (cecal intubation 96.1%; median withdrawal time 13 min), but adequate bowel preparation was below target (80.2%). Endoscopists performing ≥1 surveillance/month had higher adjusted polyp detection (used as a surrogate marker of mucosal inspection quality rather than true dysplasia) (odds ratio [OR] 1.26), and procedures allocated extended time had higher detection (OR 1.40). These findings suggest that regular exposure to IBD surveillance, adequate procedural time, and consistent use/documentation of dye-based chromoendoscopy are associated with higher polyp detection during IBD surveillance colonoscopy. Importantly, these findings relate to polyp detection rather than histologically confirmed dysplasia detection. Further work is required to determine whether service concentration or minimum surveillance volumes improve dysplasia-related outcomes. Service-level pathways analogous to English Bowel Cancer Screening with national standards and performance monitoring may warrant consideration.

items.title: Parathyroid Hormone-related Peptide Is a Better Indicator of Cancer Treatment Efficacy Than Serum Calcium.
items.abstract: Cancer-associated hypercalcemia is commonly a paraneoplastic manifestation of ectopic parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) production. Although serum calcium is routinely monitored, it can be influenced by antiresorptive therapy, albumin concentration, vitamin D status, and other clinical factors. Because durable control of hypercalcemia depends on effective anticancer therapy, serial PTHrP measurement may provide a more direct marker of treatment efficacy than serum calcium alone. A 66-year-old woman with extensive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) of the scalp was considered unsuitable for primary surgical extirpation and was treated with the immune checkpoint inhibitor cemiplimab. While awaiting insurance approval, she was hospitalized with severe hypercalcemia. After one course of cemiplimab, both serum calcium and PTHrP were mildly elevated. After the second course, serum calcium fell to the low-normal range, whereas PTHrP rose markedly. Subsequent imaging showed rapid progression with metastases to the bone, brain, lung, and liver, and the patient died shortly thereafter. In progressive malignancy, PTHrP detected by immunoassay may increase even when serum calcium normalizes or declines. This case suggests that serial PTHrP levels may be more informative than serum calcium alone for assessing anticancer treatment efficacy in PTHrP-mediated hypercalcemia.

items.title: Overall Survival After Neoadjuvant Versus Adjuvant Chemotherapy for Invasive Urothelial Carcinoma of the Bladder: A Real-world Multicenter Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Invasive urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder carries a high risk of micrometastatic spread, and perioperative chemotherapy is a key component of curative-intent treatment. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) has the strongest supporting evidence, whereas the role of adjuvant chemotherapy (AC) remains debated and real-world comparisons are limited. We compared overall survival (OS) and the development of liver metastasis between patients treated with NAC and those treated with AC who underwent radical cystectomy. Using the TriNetX U.S. Collaborative Network, we identified adults with bladder cancer who underwent radical cystectomy and received cisplatin or carboplatin within 1 year before (NAC) or within 1 year after (AC) surgery. The two cohorts were balanced by 1:1 propensity score-matching for age, sex, and race. OS (primary endpoint) and time to liver metastasis (secondary endpoint) were estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method and compared with the log-rank test. After matching, 402 patients were included in each group. Median OS was 2,136 days for the AC group and was not reached for the NAC group. NAC was associated with significantly longer OS than AC (hazard ratio=0.528, 95% confidence interval=0.413-0.676, p p <0.0001). In this real-world cohort, NAC was associated with significantly longer OS and a lower risk of liver metastasis than AC in patients undergoing radical cystectomy for invasive bladder cancer. These hypothesis-generating findings support the preferential use of NAC when feasible and warrant prospective validation.
